title: Greedy Algorithms
summary: Building a solution one locally best choice at a time - when greedy works and how to prove it with an exchange argument, interval scheduling by earliest finish time, counting meeting rooms with a sweep, why greedy coin change fails for some coin systems, Huffman coding with a priority queue, the fractional knapsack, and a checklist for spotting greedy problems.

cards.q: For interval scheduling with one room, which greedy rule always gives the most meetings?
cards.a:
earliest finish first

Finishing early leaves the most room for everything else; the exchange argument proves it.

cards.q: With coins 1, 3 and 4, what does "largest coin first" pay for 6?
cards.a:
4 + 1 + 1

Greedy takes three coins, though 3 + 3 uses two: a greedy choice can block a better combination, so this coin system needs dynamic programming.

cards.q: In Huffman coding, which two items are merged at each step?
cards.a:
the two least frequent

Merging the rarest items pushes them deepest, so they get the longest codes.
